title: How to Assess a Rent-Free Lease Incentive
excerpt: Rent-free periods can help with establishment costs, but they should be assessed with the whole lease proposal and documented clearly.
author: Joe Kelley
metaDescription: Learn how to assess and document a rent-free period as part of the total commercial lease proposal.
body:
A rent-free period is one form of lease incentive. Its value depends on how it is calculated, when it applies and what the rest of the lease requires.

## Start with the business need

Identify establishment costs, fitout timing and cash-flow pressure. An incentive should support the occupancy plan rather than distract from unsuitable premises or weak lease terms.

## Compare the whole proposal

Model rent, outgoings, reviews, fitout contributions, parking, security and make-good alongside the incentive. A larger headline incentive does not automatically make a proposal better.

## Clarify the mechanics

Confirm whether the relief applies to base rent only or other charges, whether it is taken at the start or spread through the term, and what happens if dates or works change.

## Link it to verified timing

Map access, approvals, landlord works, tenant works and trading commencement. Avoid relying on an incentive period that may expire while the premises cannot be used.

## Record the agreement properly

The commercial agreement should be reflected consistently in the lease and any incentive deed. Ask a commercial property lawyer to review the documents and consequences of default, assignment or early termination.
